# kener_site_config (Resource)

Manages a single Kener global site-configuration value (e.g. `title`, `siteName`, `theme`, `nav`). These keys are a fixed set that can only be updated, not created or deleted: applying this resource sets the key's value, and destroying it removes the key from Terraform state while leaving the value on the server unchanged.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A string-valued key.
resource "kener_site_config" "site_name" {
  key   = "siteName"
  value = jsonencode("Example Status")
}

# An object-valued key (navigation links).
resource "kener_site_config" "nav" {
  key = "nav"
  value = jsonencode([
    { name = "Docs", url = "https://example.com/docs", iconURL = "" },
    { name = "Home", url = "https://example.com", iconURL = "" },
  ])
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `key` (String) The site-configuration key to manage (e.g. `title`, `siteName`, `siteURL`, `theme`, `logo`, `nav`). See the Kener docs for the full list. Changing it forces replacement.
- `value` (String) The value as JSON. Use `jsonencode(...)` — a string value is `jsonencode("My Title")`, an object/array value is `jsonencode({ ... })`. Kener may normalise object values server-side.

### Read-Only

- `data_type` (String) The value's data type as reported by Kener (`string` or `object`).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Site-config entries are imported by their key.
terraform import kener_site_config.site_name siteName
```
